body_markdown:
Fintech apps now make it easier to receive, hold, convert, and spend dollars from your phone, making it easier to open a USD account in Nigeria without visiting a bank branch or dealing with lengthy paperwork.


However, not every USD account offers the same experience. Fees, receiving methods, card options, conversion costs, and supported payment platforms can vary significantly.


If you want to open a USD account in Nigeria, compare the features that affect your money most. This guide compares seven popular options and highlights where each one stands out. Most importantly, it shows why[Cleva](http://www.getcleva.com/) is a strong choice for Nigerians who earn and spend in dollars.


## What to consider before you open a USD account in Nigeria


Before choosing an app, think about how you plan to use your account.


Receiving fees matter if you earn from international clients or platforms. A small fee on every payment can add up quickly.


You should also check withdrawal and conversion costs. Some providers charge a percentage when you convert your dollars to naira. Others may add fixed fees to specific transactions.


Card access matters too. If you pay for software, subscriptions, advertising, or other international services, a virtual dollar card can make things easier.


Finally, consider whether the account supports the platforms you already use. Freelancers may care about Upwork deposits, while businesses may need ACH or wire transfers.


With those factors in mind, here are seven apps to consider when you want to open a USD account in Nigeria.


## 1. Cleva


[Cleva](http://www.getcleva.com/) is our top pick for anyone looking to open a USD account in Nigeria and manage international money from one app.


Cleva lets you receive USD through ACH, FedNow, wire transfers, and supported stablecoins. You can also receive payments from platforms such as Upwork and Payoneer.


For Upwork users, Cleva offers free Upwork deposits. That means you can receive eligible Upwork payments without an additional Cleva deposit fee.


Cleva also keeps receiving fees competitive. ACH deposits cost between $2 and $5, depending on the transaction.


When it comes to conversion, Cleva does not charge a conversion fee. You can convert your USD to naira without an additional conversion charge from Cleva.


The Cleva Classic Card gives you another way to use your USD balance. Card creation costs $3, with no card maintenance fee. Better still, you can add the card to both Apple Pay and Google Pay. That makes it useful for subscriptions, software, online purchases, and everyday spending.


There are benefits beyond receiving and spending money, too. Cleva lets you earn Points on eligible transactions. You can redeem those Points for cash or data, giving you more value from transactions you already make. You can also save on everyday expenses directly through Cleva. Buy data at a 3% discount and pay electricity bills at a 1% discount.


For Nigerians who want to open a USD account in Nigeria, Cleva combines receiving, holding, converting, saving, spending, and rewards in one experience.


## 2. Grey


Grey is another option for people who want to open a USD account in Nigeria, particularly if they need multiple currencies.


The platform supports USD, GBP, EUR, and USDC. It also offers international receiving accounts and a virtual card.


Grey can suit freelancers and remote workers who receive money from clients abroad. However, Grey’s fees vary by transaction type. Its USD receiving fee, for example, can reach as high as $10.


## 3. Raenest


Raenest (formerly Geegpay) is designed for freelancers, creators, and remote workers who need international payment accounts. Users can receive money in USD, GBP, and EUR. The platform also offers a virtual card for international spending.


Raenest can be useful if you work with clients in different countries. Its multi-currency approach gives it an advantage for users who regularly handle more than one foreign currency. However, you should compare its fees before deciding where to open a USD account in Nigeria. Receiving and conversion costs can affect how much you keep from each payment.


## 4. Wise


Wise is one of the best-known international money platforms. It supports more than 40 currencies globally and focuses heavily on transparent exchange rates. However, Nigerian users need to check availability before relying on Wise for a USD account. Wise currently states that USD account details are unavailable in Nigeria.


That limitation makes Wise less suitable for Nigerians specifically looking to open a USD account in Nigeria. Wise remains a strong option in markets where its USD account details are available. For Nigerians, however, local availability should come first.


## 5. Payoneer


Payoneer is popular among freelancers, online sellers, and professionals who receive international payments. It supports receiving accounts in currencies including USD, GBP, and EUR. The platform also connects with several global marketplaces and payment platforms. Payoneer can work well for platform payouts. However, its fees can vary significantly depending on the transaction and payment method.


If your main goal is to open a USD account in Nigeria for marketplace or platform earnings, Payoneer is worth considering alongside other options.


## 6. Chipper Cash


Chipper Cash also offers USD account options to eligible Nigerian users.


Its USD virtual account can help users receive eligible ACH payments from US-based accounts. Chipper also offers a USD card for international spending. However, the card has both a creation fee and a monthly maintenance charge. Those recurring costs can matter if you use the card regularly.


## 7. LemFi


LemFi is another option for Nigerians who want to open a USD account in Nigeria, especially those who also need GBP. Its Global Accounts feature supports USD and GBP. Users can receive, hold, convert, and send international funds through the platform.


LemFi can be particularly useful for people who earn in both dollars and pounds. It also offers international transfers as part of its broader product. However, your choice should depend on how you receive and spend money.


## Feature Comparison


Here’s how the leading options compare on the features that matter most.

The right option depends on your income sources and how you use your money.


Grey and Geegpay stand out for users who need multiple currencies. Payoneer works well for platform payouts, while LemFi can suit people who regularly handle USD and GBP. Wise has a strong international reputation, but its USD account limitations affect Nigerian users. Chipper can work for people already using its ecosystem.


For an all-round USD experience, Cleva stands out.

## FAQs about opening a USD account in Nigeria


### 1. Can I open a USD account in Nigeria without a traditional bank?


Yes. Several fintech platforms offer digital USD accounts or wallets without requiring you to open a traditional domiciliary account.


The exact features depend on the provider. Some focus on receiving payments, while others add cards, savings, transfers, or multi-currency accounts.


### 2. What is the best app to open a USD account in Nigeria?


Cleva is a strong overall choice for Nigerians who want to open a USD account in Nigeria.

### 3. Is a USD fintech account the same as a domiciliary account?


Not necessarily. A fintech USD account can work differently from a traditional Nigerian bank domiciliary account.


Before opening an account, check the provider’s terms, supported payment methods, limits, and withdrawal options.
